problem:
Consider the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

- $A$ is lower triangular
- ${A}^{T}-A$ is lower triangular
- $A$ is upper triangular

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Correct Statements About a Matrix
examples.problem:
Consider the matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075464/assets/4dd9b1c1b3d789c166ecd8f6d2a909609c7f4324705c84115cce84a29181bf32.png)
Which of the following statements are true?

- $A$ is upper triangular

- $A$ is lower triangular

- $A^T-A$ is lower triangular
examples.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false, since $A$ has non-zero entries below the main diagonal:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075464/assets/c1ec838cd30cca8fbb2e3996d5a7d84dadb233e1951d05b532a9d606d887eb2f.png)

- Statement II is true, since all the entries above the main diagonal are zeros:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075464/assets/f39c68a9b1f5e16caffbf159b629a958e147e14099334b049bdfcd857eef84d2.png)

- Statement III is false, since the result of $A^T-A$ has non-zero entries above the main diagonal:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075464/assets/f4415c87201f5b92f23e3320c313cd58ac4e720135928645896f976614c5eaa0.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

feedback.problem:
Which of the following matrices are lower triangular matrices?

$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
The matrices $A$ and $B$ are lower triangular matrices since all the entries above the main diagonal are zeros.

The matrix $C$ is *not* a lower triangular matrix since it has a non-zero element above the main diagonal: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{12} & =-2\ne 0\end{aligned}
$$
